text:
hugo: FYI hitting widespread ContainerCreating stalls in us-west3-f during the 02:30 attach window. pods held ~20-50s. nvme %util and avgqu spiked. looks like janitor scrub buckets aligned with attach bulk.

maya: ugh. any quick node snippets?

hugo: pasted short samples from an affected host.
```
# iostat -x 1 2
Device    r/s    w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s  avgqu-sz  await  %util
nvme0n1  1500.0 3800.0 60000 480000   3.2     11.8  99.1
```
[ 4000.100] scrubber[7102]: async-scrub start nvme0n1 cohort=us-west3-f-5 bucket=17
[ 4000.105] kernel: nvme0n1: queue depth saturated, throttle
[ 4000.330] kubelet: attach timeout waiting for ephemeral disk

li: Hmm. Looks like our adaptive-bucket allocator picked the same bucket across many hosts (bucket=17). That accidental alignment can cause these spikes.

maya: short-term plan?

hugo: quick fixes I'm applying now: 1) soft pause janitor on a small canary subset: `janitorctl pause --cohort us-west3-f-5 --subset canaryA --until +20m` 2) set scrub threads to ionice -c3 on those hosts 3) apply label `ephemeral.quiet=true` so autoscaler prefers others during window.

sre-bot: [action] pause applied to us-west3-f-5/canaryA at 3169991020

fleet-bot: [info] autoscaler hint prefer_ephemeral_quiet=true applied to cohort us-west3-f-5/canaryA

li: Glad you're pausing. Medium-term: we should randomize bucket assignment across hosts and add a jitter window to scrub-scheduler so global alignment is unlikely. Also add a safeguard: if nvme_util > 90% we delay non-critical janitor tasks for X minutes automatically.

maya: Also collecting SMART logs from 4 hosts because i saw rising media_errors in the last week on some disks. command: `nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1` and `nvme error-log /dev/nvme0n1`. If we see wear+high util repeatedly we escalate to hw.

hugo: After the pause attach success on canaryA jumped 64% -> 98% in 2m. leaving monitoring for 30m and will resume scrub with staggered randomized buckets.

li: followups: RFC to: 1) add bucket-randomization and jitter in scrub-scheduler, 2) autoscaler-scrub forecast API so scrub can back off proactively, 3) automated ioprio/ionice lowering when attach waves detected, 4) SMART-monitoring integration to detect chronic wear.

maya: cost tradeoff note: pausing/staggering scrubs increases total scrub wall time (~+3-6% IO-hours) and slightly spreads wear, but avoids failed attaches that waste GPU minutes. we'll quantify in RFC.

hugo: filed TICKET-7109 with logs and smart snapshots and started RFC draft. tagging sched-team and hw-team. will post postmortem if repeats. :thumbsup:
